citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 2, From 1857 until the Fire of 1871. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885.
author: Alfred Theodore Andreas
locator: The landmark buildings of the 1871 scene, by printed page: the Court House as City Hall (the joint building of 1853, the two wings and additional storey of 1869-1870, Lockport marble and Lemont stone), p. 66; the Court House bell falling at 2:05 a.m. on 9 October, pp. 368 and 719; the Chamber of Commerce's corner-stone and completion, pp. 357-358, its description (Athens marble on the north, east and west fronts, brick on the south facing Calhoun Place, 93 by 180 feet, the triple window thirty feet high and twelve wide, the mansard twenty-three feet above the cornice), p. 358, and its burning about 1:20 a.m. on 9 October, p. 368; the Tremont House (Couch's hotel of 1850, five and a half stories, 140 feet on Lake by 180 on Dearborn, J. M. Van Osdel), pp. 501-502; the Sherman House (1861, six stories, 180 feet on Clark by 150 on Randolph overlooking the public square, Athens marble from Lemont, a little over $200,000), pp. 502-503. T-3688 adds: the Tribune Company's building on the south-east corner of Madison and Dearborn (Joliet marble, four stories, $225,000), p. 492, and its iron front frames, roof and shutters, 'considered absolutely fireproof', p. 563; the Palmer House (1869-70, north-west corner of State and Quincy, eight stories, 'handsome stone fronts', opened 26 September 1870), p. 509; Crosby's Opera House (north side of Washington Street 'nearly midway between State and Dearborn', W. W. Boyington, completed spring 1865, opened 20 April 1865), pp. 601-602; Field, Leiter & Co. at State and Washington from the autumn of 1868, pp. 694-695, and Horace White's 'massive pile of pure marble and iron' kept wet by the store's own pumps, p. 734; the Palmer House falling after daylight, p. 726; the four o'clock survivors (the Palmer House, the Tribune), p. 739.
rights_note: Published 1885 in the United States; public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-19 (T-3688) in the Internet Archive's plain-text OCR of this scan (historyofchicago02andr_djvu.txt), at the passages the locator names, with page images of the plates opened at the leaves the plates fall on; printed page numbers are read from the OCR's running heads and folios.
note: A compiled history fourteen years after the fire, built on the city's newspapers, the Board of Trade's records and the builders' own accounts, so secondary; but it is the fullest single description of the pre-fire buildings' size, stone, architects and cost, and of the hour each burned.
what_it_supplies: the size, storeys, stone, architect, cost and date of the 1871 scene's landmark buildings
when and how each burned on 8-9 October 1871
what_it_does_not_supply: measured drawings or surveyed positions: street corners only
